meta.label: Volunteering
tradeoffLabels: easy to start with a simple sign-up
little personal data or screening required to begin
meta.attribution: Facts here come from each organization's own volunteering, screening or background-check page, read directly, plus the National Park Service's official Reference Manual 7 for its Volunteers-in-Parks program. Accessibility describes how much stands between deciding to help and actually starting: an application, an interview, a minimum term, a criminal history check. Privacy describes how much personal data that route requires you to hand over to begin, from just an email address up to a Social Security number and fingerprints. Neither score is a judgment of the organization's mission or the value of the work; a route that screens hard usually does so because it puts volunteers in sustained, unsupervised contact with children, elderly people or people with disabilities, and the screening exists to protect them, not to inconvenience the volunteer. Several organizations run tiered systems where a single event needs almost nothing and an ongoing or higher-trust role needs a full background check; where that is true, the note says so and the score reflects the more common, lower-commitment route into that organization. Two entries, DoSomething.org and JustServe, plus Idealist, describe their own sign-up process as an account and a listing, with no screening step described at the platform level; that description is the evidence for a high score, not an audit of the thousands of organizations each one lists. Ways to help describes the breadth of distinct opportunities a route actually offers, which is unscored wherever no organization published a concrete figure for it. Giving money instead of time is a different decision, covered under Causes to support and Crowdfunding platforms. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: Easy to start, without a lengthy application or minimum term
Little personal data or background screening required to begin
Breadth of distinct volunteer opportunities on offer

products.name: Idealist (formerly VolunteerMatch)
products.description: A merged nonprofit and volunteer-opportunity board, after VolunteerMatch became part of Idealist in early 2025. Lists a large number of listings across many cause areas, virtual and in person, through a free account.

accessibility.note: Idealist's VolunteerMatch page states VolunteerMatch became part of Idealist 'in early 2025' and describes finding opportunities and applying through the site; volunteermatch.org itself now redirects permanently to this Idealist page.

ways_to_help.note: The page states the combined platform offers '100,000+ unique ways to volunteer, with opportunities for virtual and onsite opportunities to support 56 different cause areas.'

products.name: JustServe
products.description: A free volunteer-matching site and app run by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, open to anyone regardless of faith, connecting people to local community service projects posted by other organizations.

accessibility.note: JustServe's about page states 'JustServe is free for all users, organizations and volunteers' and that creating an account is done through the website or app, with the site stating 'everyone is invited to use JustServe, regardless of their race, religion, gender, ethnicity, or sexual orientation.'

privacy.note: The about page describes registering an account and customizing a profile to match skills and interests with posted projects; it does not describe a background check or other screening step at the JustServe platform level, distinct from whatever the individual project's host organization may separately require.

products.name: AmeriCorps
products.description: A US national service program placing members in full-time or part-time community roles for a set term, with a living allowance and an education award in return. Positions with recurring access to children, older adults or people with disabilities require a criminal history check before service starts.

accessibility.note: AmeriCorps' own National Service Criminal History Checks page states three checks are required before an eligible person may begin serving: a National Sex Offender Public Website check, a state criminal history check, and an FBI fingerprint-based check, all completed and reviewed no later than the day before service begins.

privacy.note: The same page states the process includes an FBI fingerprint-based check conducted through an AmeriCorps-approved vendor, and that applicants submit a copy of government-issued identification along with a set of fingerprints as part of the National Service Criminal History Check.

ways_to_help.note: The page's own navigation lists several distinct AmeriCorps program tracks that fall under national service, including AmeriCorps State/National, AmeriCorps VISTA, and AmeriCorps Seniors' RSVP, Foster Grandparent and Senior Companion programs, each with its own eligibility path.

products.name: Peace Corps
products.description: A US federal program placing volunteers abroad for a roughly 27-month assignment across sectors including agriculture, education, health, environment and community development. Every invitee goes through a background investigation and a full medical clearance before departing.

accessibility.note: Peace Corps' legal clearance page states 'the Peace Corps is required to complete a background investigation on all applicants' and that once conditionally invited, an applicant receives 'guidance on submitting fingerprints and the background investigation certification form' before they can depart for service.

privacy.note: The same page states full disclosure of legal history is required, including any citation, arrest or charge regardless of outcome, and that fingerprints are submitted as part of the background investigation certification process; non-disclosure alone can result in a rescinded invitation.

ways_to_help.note: The Peace Corps site's own navigation lists six work sectors volunteers are placed in: Agriculture, Community Economic Development, Education, Environment, Health, and Youth in Development.

products.name: Habitat for Humanity
products.description: Builds and repairs homes with volunteer labor alongside future homeowners. Most build-day volunteers only need to register and sign a waiver; a background check applies to four specific roles, including trip team leaders and Disaster Corps volunteers.

accessibility.note: Habitat for Humanity International's own background-check FAQ states the screening policy adopted June 1, 2019 applies specifically to '(1) trip team leaders, (2) Care-A-Vanners, (3) Disaster Corps volunteers and (4) AmeriCorps host site managers,' meaning most day-to-day build volunteers are not in a role the policy covers.

privacy.note: For the roles the policy does cover, the same document states an applicant provides 'full legal name, date of birth, social security number, phone number, email and address history' to Habitat's background-check vendor Asurint, so most build-day volunteers outside those four roles are not asked for this information.

ways_to_help.note: The same document names five distinct volunteer pathways with different screening rules: general build volunteers, trip team leaders, Care-A-Vanners, Disaster Corps volunteers, and AmeriCorps host site managers.

products.name: American Red Cross
products.description: Runs disaster response, blood drives and safety training through local volunteers. Applying means creating a Volunteer Connection profile, and a background check is a standard step before a role is assigned, not a special case.

accessibility.note: The Red Cross's Virginia volunteer FAQ, on the national redcross.org domain, describes the steps as entering a zip code, applying to an opportunity, creating a Volunteer Connection account, and states 'once you have completed the application process and background check, a volunteer Engagement Specialist will contact you' to finalize a match.

privacy.note: The same FAQ states disaster response applicants 'will also be required to submit a background check' as part of the standard application through Volunteer Connection, ahead of being matched with an Engagement Specialist.

products.name: Special Olympics
products.description: Provides year-round sports training and competition for people with intellectual disabilities. Volunteers with regular, close athlete contact go through a full criminal background check; day-of-event volunteers with limited, supervised contact only complete a registration form and a photo ID check.

accessibility.note: Special Olympics Texas's published Volunteer Screening Policy, which it adopts to implement the national US Volunteer Screening Policy set by Special Olympics, Inc., states Class B volunteers, defined as day-of-event volunteers with limited, supervised athlete contact, need only 'submit a signed, completed, and truthful Class B Registration Form' and pass a photo-ID check at the event, with no criminal background check required for that tier.

privacy.note: The same policy states Class A volunteers, those with regular close contact or a position of trust or authority, must 'complete and pass a criminal background check through Verified Volunteers' at Level 3 screening, while Class B day-of-event volunteers submit only a registration form with name, address and phone number and are not put through that criminal-history process.

links.label: Volunteer Screening Policy (Special Olympics Texas, implementing the SOI national policy)

products.name: DoSomething.org
products.description: A campaign platform for people age 13 to 25 to take specific social-change actions on climate, safety and equity, ranging from short one-time actions to sustained projects, with no age ceiling enforced beyond the stated range.

accessibility.note: DoSomething's about page states 'if you're 13-25, there's a space for you at our table' and describes the platform as a coach, champion and connector helping members take pledges and complete actions and campaigns.

privacy.note: The about page describes taking a pledge and completing a documented action, such as an 'action streak,' as the participation model; it does not describe a background check or screening step for taking part in a campaign.

products.name: Big Brothers Big Sisters
products.description: Matches an adult volunteer mentor with a child for a sustained one-on-one relationship. Becoming a mentor means a written application, reference checks, an in-person interview and a background check before being matched.

accessibility.note: Big Brothers Big Sisters of America's national safeguarding page states its 'National Standards of Excellence require each volunteer to complete an extensive screening process,' naming a written application, background and reference checks, and an in-person interview as required steps before a match, on top of orientation and training.

privacy.note: The same page confirms background and reference checks are a required part of that national screening process for every volunteer, in addition to the in-person interview, before a mentoring match is made.

products.name: National Park Service Volunteers-in-Parks
products.description: Places volunteers in national parks for anything from a single trail day to a long-term assignment. Short-term, episodic volunteering uses a simpler sign-up form; longer assignments can call for more paperwork, including background checks for certain roles.

accessibility.note: The NPS's Reference Manual 7, Chapter 5, distinguishes short-term or episodic volunteering, which uses the simpler OF301a individual form (or OF301b for a group led by one signed form), from long-term volunteering, and states that after the volunteer service agreement is signed, a park 'may require the volunteer's signature on additional written documentation or forms that pertain to their assignment,' including background-check forms.

privacy.note: The same chapter states additional forms tied to a specific assignment 'may include forms for background checks, PIV issuance, vehicle usage, credentialing, training certifications,' indicating background screening applies to some roles and assignments rather than to every Volunteers-in-Parks sign-up.

links.label: Reference Manual 7, Chapter 5: Onboarding and Management

products.name: Meals on Wheels America
products.description: Connects people to a local Meals on Wheels provider to deliver meals to homebound neighbors, usually using the volunteer's own car. Screening is set locally rather than nationally, so what is required varies by provider.

accessibility.note: Meals on Wheels America's volunteer page states the sign-up step is to 'fill out the signup form above, and we'll share contact information for a local Meals on Wheels provider in your area,' after which the volunteer contacts that provider directly to discuss the role.

privacy.note: The same page states 'the vetting process for volunteers varies by location,' and that volunteers 'may be asked to undergo a background check process prior to volunteering,' so the personal information required is set by the local provider rather than being uniform nationwide.

products.name: Points of Light
products.description: A global network of affiliate volunteer-mobilizing organizations, searchable by region and cause through its own engagement platform, connecting people to opportunities run by its member organizations rather than running programs itself.

accessibility.note: Points of Light's global network page states people can 'find a volunteer opportunity or start a project' through its engagement platform, engage.pointsoflight.org, with opportunities filterable by region, country and the services each member organization offers.

ways_to_help.note: The page states the network comprises 'more than 120 affiliates across 32 countries around the world' and that it engaged approximately 3 million volunteers in 2024.
